notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/imswitch2__imswitch2 --backend fake (exit 0; evidence contract_checked, not an MHS-Device level). check-report.json has no findings and is regenerated by every gate run. The card lists five entry symbols for the ImSwitch2 application; this package implements one device, imswitch.imcontrol.model.managers.rotators.StandaRotatorManager:StandaRotatorManager, the Standa 8SMC5 motor controller for a motorized rotation mount. NidaqManager, RecordingManager, Cobolt06 and Cobolt06DPL are other parts of the application and are named in facts.md but are not part of this package. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the package is a direct Driver with a native.py factory instead of the PythonObjectDriver helper, because the absolute move needs a rad-to-degrees conversion before the native call and a read-back after the manager's blocking move_abs, and the stop is a native controller command. NOT COVERED: continuous rotation (start_cont_rot), relative move (move_rel), speed write (set_rot_speed, mrpm), software zero (set_zero_pos), sync-in settings (set_sync_in_set) and get_info; only the position read, the absolute move (cap.motion.joint_position.v1), the stop (cap.motion.stop.v1) and the e-stop are exposed. No text file of the clone states the travel range of the mount, so joint_positions is Limit.operator_required and every move is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator supplies an envelope; site-limits.example.json is an example, not a statement about any unit. The stop action accepts the class's optional deceleration and ignores it: the controller's stop command takes no profile argument. The fake is package-local rather than the upstream simulator: the card's mock_strategy hints name image-array simulators for detector data, and the only upstream stand-in for this device, MockStandaMotor, is the motor interface, not the manager, and lacks the manager's stop and position interface. The fake models only the members the driver uses (get_pos, position, move_abs, stop_cont_rot, close); it has no motion over time, speed, continuous rotation or controller errors. Nothing here ran on hardware: native.py and the upstream imswitch package were never imported or executed, and no hardware run is claimed. The package is R1 and model-authored with reviewed_by null, so the loader does not refuse its hardware backend on review grounds; the backend remains an operator decision.
